title.en: Beatles as students of American pop
title.zh: 作为美式流行乐学生的Beatles

summary.en: The so-called British Invasion was largely a study of American pop; the Beatles are the prime example.
summary.zh: 所谓的“英伦入侵（British Invasion）”，很大程度上是对美式流行乐的学习，The Beatles就是代表。

body.zh:
我想多花点时间讲讲The Beatles。在1964年之后这段时期，可以看到一些变化在许多乐队身上发生，The Beatles可以作为这些变化的代表。这应该是一种成长，我认为是一种艺术手法，或者说音乐的真实意志（authenticity in music）。

我们首先要把披头士看做一个美式流行乐的学习者。当你听到媒体都在使用，且一直使用“英伦入侵 (British Invasion) ”这个词语时，你会觉得英伦入侵的音乐是根植于英国本土音乐。但是当你从学者或者音乐分析家的角度，从结构上看这个时期的音乐，弄明白这些音乐的内涵，及其影响、技法和结构时，你会发现这时期90%或95%的音乐本质上都是美式流行乐。当然了，是带有浓重英伦腔的美式流行乐，但其本质还是美式流行乐。因此在很多方面看来，我认为The Beatles毫无疑问是美国流行乐的学习者。我们了解到，大多数英国音乐人都很推崇美式音乐，而且很想要模仿美式流行乐，认为英国人确实可以做得和美国人一样好。那为什么The Beatles不能是美式流行乐的学习者呢？

作为学者，我们是怎么知道他们熟悉，或者说谙熟这种1955到1962、63年间的美式流行乐呢？我们知道他们在德国汉堡所做的，知道他们演奏了什么。学者们尽可能地找到The Beatles翻唱过的歌曲表，找到他们的演出录音记录，不是在汉堡的那些演出记录，是他们按照在汉堡的演出为BBC录的音，因此我们可以听听他们是怎样演绎这些歌曲的。他们不想把打算在唱片中发行的材料直接给BBC，但是他们又太忙了，顾不上把这些歌曲重新排练一遍。我们可以听到这些录音材料。有一些关于The Beatles的书，记录了大约从1960或1961直到解散，他们每天都在做些什么。如果你看这些书，你一定会很惊讶，这些家伙每天都在演出、录音、上电视或者有其他杂七杂八的安排，所以当他们排练个新版本时，或许并不是，他们只是把那些老东西吹吹灰了，然后拿出来表演。

这些老东西有很多，我们从中听出他们对这些曲调的演绎和原唱片十分相像。如果你去找他们在BBC录音的那首《That's Alright Mama》，你或许可以拿着它骗过一个Elvis Presley的歌迷，说这是Elvis Presley在Sun Records或者某场演出的版本。Paul McCartney听起来跟Elvis Presley一样，如果你知道Paul McCartney这个人，你能从声音辨别出这是Paul McCartney在唱，但如果你不知道他，这听起来就和Elvis Presley没什么区别了。George Harrison的吉他solo也和Scotty Moore在唱片里演绎的一样。当你听着这些BBC录音时，你能听到一首接一首像这样和原版相近的版本，由此看来，他们知道美式流行乐是怎么一回事，他们翻唱了一些50年代末到60年代的组合：Carl Perkins、The Coasters、The Cookies和The Shirelles（后两者是女子组合），还有Elvis Presley、Chuck Berry、Buddy Holly、Ray Charles等一些Motown旗下艺人等等。他们确实是对美式音乐理解通透的学习者，不仅仅理解了其曲调如何，还理解了它们的曲调走向和编排。因此，当他们开始写自己的歌，做着百年来创作者做的事，作为年轻的词曲作者，他们就以他们熟稔的音乐作为范本写歌。

到美国接受采访的时候，他们多少也承认了这点。有一次采访Paul McCartney时问道，展望未来，你看到了什么？他的回答大概是，John和我作为一个歌曲创作团队，这次表演让The Beatles风靡一时，他们认为这影响也就能持续一两年，之后他们会为其他艺人写歌，他们把自己看作是Leiber & Stoller那样的词曲团队，这就是他们对自己的定位。对于了解并可以深刻理解美式词曲传统这件事，他们十分自豪。所以他们很多歌曲里，美式音乐的影响不仅体现在制作的价值观、技术和乐器编排方面，也体现在音乐结构上。

现在我们要重点看看Beatles是怎样从这种工匠式的模仿中走出来的，工匠式的模仿指的是熟练于制作一首又一首的流行歌曲，就像之前讲过的Brill Building里制作出来的东西。他们是怎样从60年代的套路中走出，变得更像艺术家呢？当你不想一遍又一遍地重复同样的事时，就会想不断尝试新鲜事物，去超越流行乐边界、突破流行乐的可能。这就使得他们从匠人变成了艺术家，从而创造了流行乐中新的审美，这种审美将成为此后摇滚乐对真实性的一种态度。
body.en:
I want more time on the Beatles. After 1964 you can see changes in many bands; the Beatles can stand for those changes. It should be a kind of growth—what I think of as an artistic approach, or authenticity in music.

First we should see the Beatles as students of American pop. When you hear the media use—and keep using—“British Invasion,” you may think Invasion music is rooted in native British music. But when you look as a scholar or analyst—structure, content, influence, technique—you find that about 90% or 95% of this period’s music is essentially American pop. Of course American pop with a thick British accent, but still American pop at heart. So in many ways I think the Beatles are undoubtedly students of American pop. We know most British musicians admired American music and wanted to imitate it, believing the British could do as well as Americans. Why should the Beatles not be students of American pop?

As scholars, how do we know they knew—really knew—American pop from about 1955 to 1962–63? We know what they did in Hamburg and what they played. Scholars have compiled lists of songs they covered and performance recordings—not only Hamburg, but BBC sessions that followed the Hamburg set lists—so we can hear how they played them. They did not want to give the BBC material they planned to release on record, but they were too busy to re-rehearse everything. We can hear those tapes. Some Beatles books track almost day by day from about 1960 or 1961 to the breakup. If you read them you will be surprised how often they were performing, recording, on TV, or otherwise booked—so when they “rehearsed a new version,” maybe they just dusted off old numbers and played them.

There is a lot of that old material; their readings sound very close to the original records. If you find their BBC “That’s All Right Mama,” you might fool an Elvis fan into thinking it is Elvis at Sun or in a live show. Paul McCartney sounds like Elvis; if you know Paul you can tell it is him, but if you do not, it is hard to separate from Elvis. George Harrison’s guitar solo matches Scotty Moore on the record. Listening to these BBC sessions you hear cover after cover this close to the originals—so they knew how American pop worked. They covered late-1950s to early-1960s acts: Carl Perkins, the Coasters, the Cookies and the Shirelles (girl groups), Elvis, Chuck Berry, Buddy Holly, Ray Charles, Motown artists, and more. They were students who really understood American music—not only how the tunes went, but arrangement and shape. So when they began writing their own songs—doing what songwriters have done for ages—as young writers they used the music they knew as models.

In American interviews they partly admitted this. Asked what he saw ahead, Paul roughly said that John and he as a songwriting team had made the Beatles a craze that might last a year or two, then they would write for other artists—seeing themselves as a Leiber & Stoller-type team. That was their self-image. They were proud of knowing and deeply understanding the American songwriting tradition. So in many of their songs American influence shows not only in production values, technique, and instrumentation, but in musical structure.

Now we focus on how the Beatles moved out of craftsman-style imitation—skill at turning out hit after hit like Brill Building product. How did they leave 1960s formulas and become more like artists? When you do not want to repeat the same thing again and again, you keep trying new things—to push past pop’s borders and what pop can do. That is how they went from craftsmen to artists, creating a new aesthetic in pop that would become rock’s later attitude toward authenticity.
